stories.headline: RTC should do more with Gamyam bus live-tracking app
stories.deck: “The RTC should ensure newer routes are updated as soon as they’re launched”
stories.bodyText:
Bus users have pointed out that the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation’s (TGSRTC) bus tracking app, Gamyam, has not been as effective as they had hoped, with concerns over live tracking, route information and the punctuality of services.
Sharing his experience, Prithvi Raj, a student and bus user, said there had been some occasions when he was unable to track in real time the bus he intended to board .
“RTC should ensure that Gamyam should not be limited to displaying bus locations. Data should be used to monitor whether buses are adhering to timetables, identify consistently delayed services, and improve punctuality. Another concern is that some buses are skipping designated bus stops and operating like express services instead of ordinary services. Such behaviour should be monitored through the app, and action should be taken,” he said.
The concerns come even as the TGSRTC has sanctioned ₹19.21 crore for the vehicle tracking and passenger information system, according to a response to a Right to Information (RTI) request filed by Kareem Ansari through the portal YOURTI.in.
According to the letter of award, the negotiated rate for the vehicle tracking and passenger information system is ₹375 per bus per month, excluding GST.
The rollout initially covered 4,170 buses and was subsequently extended. The corporation listed a total of 9,320 vehicles till March.
Transport researchers familiar with the system said the TGSRTC needed to ensure that route information was updated promptly to improve the app’s effectiveness. The corporation should inform the vendor of new routes on the day operations commence and ensure that these are reflected in the app, they added. Routes that are no longer operational should also be removed.
“The corporation should ensure that buses are mapped to the correct schedules before they leave the depot. Often, some buses are shown on a particular route but are operating on a different route,” a transport expert told The Hindu.
The expert also pointed out that route codes should be distinct even when a service terminates short of its usual destination or is extended by just one stop.
“For example, 195W terminating at JNTU cannot be coded as 195W. It should be coded as 195J,” he said.
Apart from improving the accuracy of route information, users said the app could be made more useful by introducing features to help passengers plan journeys involving transfers between buses.
“The app does not allow filtering by route direction when searching by route. Both directions are displayed simultaneously, which confuses passengers,” said Md. Shoaib, a media professional.

stories.headline: 3 killed as two helicopters collide mid-air near Oregon airport in US
stories.bodyText:
Three people were killed after two helicopters collided mid-air near an airport in northwest Oregon on Thursday afternoon, according to the Yamhill County Sheriff's Office.
The collision occurred around 2:15 pm local time near McMinnville Municipal Airport, about 40 miles southwest of Portland. Emergency responders, including local law enforcement, firefighters and medical personnel, rushed to the scene.
One of the helicopters was carrying two people, a flight instructor from Texas and a student pilot from the United Kingdom, Yamhill County Sheriff Sam Elliott said during a news conference on Thursday evening. The second helicopter had only one occupant, a pilot from Newberg, Oregon, the sheriff said.
The sheriff's office urged the public to avoid the area and have “patience as we respond to this critical incident.”
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) was leading the investigation into the collision, with the FAA also probing the incident.
One of the helicopters involved was operated by Jerry Trimble Helicopters, a flight training school and private helicopter rental service. 
The company confirmed that one of its aircraft was involved in the incident.
“Jerry Trimble Helicopters is deeply saddened to confirm that one of our aircraft was involved in an aviation incident this afternoon,” the company said in a statement. “… Our hearts and thoughts are with the individuals involved, their families, and everyone affected by this event.”

Tirupati district tightens security for free, fair local elections
briefs.deck: Strengthening policing by arranging special deployment in sensitive and violence-prone areas, the district administration has appealed to the voters to exercise their franchise without fear
briefs.bodyText:
Tirupati District Collector S. Venkateswar has announced that all arrangements are in place for conducting the ensuing local body elections in a free and fair manner.
Strengthening policing by arranging special deployment in sensitive and violence-prone areas, the district administration has appealed to the voters to exercise their franchise without fear.
Addressing a media conference here on Thursday along with Superintendent of Police L. Subbarayudu, Joint Collector R. Govinda Rao and Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) Commissioner M. Jayakrishna, the Collector said he had reviewed every aspect of the election, including the preparedness of ballot boxes, ballot papers, security at the strong rooms, identification of polling agents, training to the staff on election duty, CCTV and video recording, transportation of ballot boxes after polling etc.
He categorically told the Presiding Officers (PO), Assistant Presiding Officers (APO) and the Other Presiding Officers (OPO) to attend the election duty as scheduled and abstaining from their duty would be viewed seriously.
Hinting at the presence of striking force at select locations to tackle trouble mongers, Mr. Subbarayudu warned the anti-social elements not to meddle with the election process or be prepared to face trouble.
A radius of 100m from the polling station would be thoroughly guarded, with restrictions on entry, lining and lighting arrangements, and as such, any violation will be viewed seriously, he added.
Earlier, the Collector conducted a video conference with officials drawn from revenue, police, municipal administration and rural development to review the arrangements made for the ensuing municipal and MPTC/ZPTC elections.

briefs.headline: Telangana spotlight: Women blast through the mining barriers
briefs.deck: From handling explosives and repairing heavy mining equipment to supervising underground operations and training to drive 100-tonne dumpers, women at State-owned Singareni Collieries Company Limited are moving into jobs long considered a male preserve after amendments to the Mines Act helped open up these opportunities to them. However, challenges remain, including workplace safety, gender bias…
briefs.bodyText:
For three-and-a-half years, Tumram Priya’s working day began with meticulous grooming, donning a crisp uniform and preparing for a day in the skies. As a flight attendant, she checked safety arrangements and ensured passengers’ comfort. Today, the 27-year-old manages personnel and vehicles at an office near an opencast coal mine in a remote, forested corner of Telangana. She is also familiar with the handling of controlled explosives.
“My father, Jaganath, worked for the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) and took voluntary retirement due to health issues. I subsequently got the job under the dependent quota,” says Priya, a commerce graduate.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu's party claims election 'stolen' as results show him losing majority
briefs.deck: Israeli media reported that members of Mr. Netanyahu's party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group
briefs.bodyText:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance, as final results showed his bloc had lost its majority in parliament.
The opposition accused Mr. Netanyahu of demonising the Arab population after a historic showing by Arab-led parties in an attempt to delegitimise the election. If the rest of the opposition teams up with Arab parties, a rare and politically risky move, they could potentially form a majority government in parliament, the Knesset.
Results released by election officials on Thursday (October 29, 2026) showed Mr. Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member assembly, well below the 68 seats it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament. His main opposition won 48 seats and Arab-led parties secured the other 19.
The count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to the country's president next Wednesday (October 28).
Mr. Netanyahu's party, Likud, has been spreading claims of malfeasance by Arab-led parties since exit polls indicated the Prime Minister had suffered a setback in Tuesday's (October 27) vote. But it ramped up the rhetoric after the head of Israel's election committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said that “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought before him.
In a letter to the Shin Bet security agency, Mr. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims. But given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.
Mr. Netanyahu's party responded with an inflammatory statement: "The elections in Israel have been stolen!” it said, claiming — without evidence — that the alleged election interference was “aimed at facilitating a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamisation of Israel and toppling of the right wing government.”
Israeli media reported that members of Mr. Netanyahu's party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group.
Qatar issued a quick denial, calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous.”
As it announced its results early on Wednesday (October 28), the election commission said the investigation was based on classified intelligence. It did not elaborate but warned of “unfounded” reports surrounding the probe.
“It does not affect the final results that will be submitted to the President, nor does it concern any particular sector of the population,” it said.
Netanyahu’s opponents accuse him of undermining vote
Mr. Netanyahu's main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said Likud was trying to delegitimise the results. “They are doing this because they lost,” he said.
Mr. Eisenkot ridiculed the accusation of foreign interference with a tongue-in-cheek statement, saying: “I welcome the fact that Netanyahu is finally condemning Qatari involvement in the State of Israel.”
Mr. Netanyahu has long faced accusations that former top aides of his accepted money from Qatar.
By casting doubt on the vote, Mr. Netanyahu appeared to be positioning himself to block any potential alliance between his opponents and the Arab parties. Mr. Netanyahu has suggested that it would be treasonous for Mr. Eisenkot to join with Arab parties.
The projected outcome of the results was expected to show both Mr. Netanyahu's bloc of religious and nationalist allies and his more secular and socially liberal opponents falling short of a parliamentary majority required to form a new government. The Arab parties would hold the remaining seats and could potentially give Mr. Eisenkot the backing he needs to oust Mr. Netanyahu.
The Shin Bet, seeking to calm tensions, said its investigation was not meant to “cast aspersions” on an entire section of the population that "exercised its right to vote in a democratic and lawful manner.”
The elections committee also sounded a note of caution in a letter written to a concerned member of parliament. It said that even though an investigation was taking place, “allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity are baseless.”
The committee wants findings from the Shin Bet within the week. Israeli law requires election results to be certified by November 4.
Netanyahu campaigned on anti-Arab sentiment
Even ahead of the vote, Mr. Netanyahu and Likud painted the Arab-led parties as a danger to Israel, which critics called an attempt to further marginalize Arab citizens. Arab citizens of Palestinian descent make up 20% of the population but are often viewed with suspicion because of their sympathies with other Palestinians.
Those campaign attacks, along with anger over the divisive Mr. Netanyahu and his far-right government, brought outraged Arabs to the polls like never before.
On Thursday (October 29), Yair Golan, head of the Democrats party, accused Mr. Netanyahu of “attempting to undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimization campaign directed against the will of the public — and against the Arab public in particular.”
“Netanyahu is working to steal the election,” the Arab-led Joint List party asserted on Thursday (October 29).
The head of the Arab-led Ra'am party, Mansour Abbas, welcomed the investigation into election interference and said his party had nothing to do with the case, while accusing Mr. Netanyahu of a campaign of incitement.
President Isaac Herzog called it a “sensitive moment” and called for a full investigation. He warned that “we must not tarnish an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.”
Difficult decisions ahead as parties seek coalitions
The developments amplified the difficult decisions for the weeks ahead. Those include whether some Jewish and Arab parties would team up in a historic alliance, or whether some parties that campaigned on ousting Mr. Netanyahu would toss that aside and join forces with him.
While the race for a 61-seat majority needed to control the 120-seat Knesset plays out, Mr. Netanyahu remains in charge.
If Mr. Netanyahu loses office, that would set off a cascade of events that critics say he has desperately sought to avoid. He would be taken to account over yearslong corruption allegations, and an inquiry almost certainly would begin into the security failures that led to the devastating Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack.
Eisenkot leaves door open to cooperation with Arab-led parties
Even without a role in a coalition, Arab-led parties could assert their growing power by supporting other Mr. Netanyahu opponents in the next parliament. That could include electing a new speaker, giving them control of the agenda and potentially allowing them to advance and pass legislation before a new government is formed.
Mr. Eisenkot has indicated he is open, with conditions, to joining forces with the Arab-led parties. Ahmad Tibi, second on the Arab-led Joint List, told Army Radio the opposition bloc reached out to him to discuss replacing the Knesset speaker, and he told them the party would support the bloc's candidate.
There were small rallies overnight in Tel Aviv, and in far more conservative Jerusalem, in support of a coalition that includes Arab-led parties. Until 2021, no Arab party had joined a coalition government, and that was brief.
If a new government cannot be formed after multiple attempts, Israel would face a new election early next year. On Wednesday (October 28), Mr. Herzog signalled he wanted to avoid that step — something Mr. Eisenkot has said as well.
New elections bring new questions, including whether Arab citizens would again go to the polls in large numbers and whether the tens of thousands of Israelis who flew home to vote would do it again. Many had said they took that step to save the country from Mr. Netanyahu.

briefs.headline: ECI extends SIR timelines in Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra, Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland
briefs.deck: The revisions follow requests from the Chief Electoral Officers of the concerned States
briefs.bodyText:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday (October 29, 2026) revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, and Nagaland.
The revisions follow requests from the Chief Electoral Officers of the concerned States.
The poll panel wrote separately to the five States and the Union Territory of Delhi about extending the timelines.
In Maharashtra, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended from October 26 to November 13.
The notice phase and disposal of claims will now run until November 25, and the final roll will be published on November 30. The draft roll came out on August 31, and disposals had previously been fixed for November 10.
In Delhi, claims and objections can now be filed until November 25, instead of October 30. Disposal of claims has been pushed from November 30 to December 15, and the final roll will be published on December 22.
The schedule for the SIR exercise has been pushed on multiple occasions in the past due to a variety of reasons.

stories.headline: Bitter cheer: Hoteliers in Bengaluru mull price revisions as Rs 8 milk price hike adds to input costs
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Your morning cuppa — at home or at an eatery — is set to leave a bitter taste, with hotels and eateries across Bengaluru preparing for a hike in beverage and food prices following govt’s decision to increase milk prices by Rs 8 per litre from Nov 1.
Hoteliers said the milk price revision comes at a time when they are already struggling with rising costs of rice, sugar, coffee powder, cooking gas and other essentials. “We have been absorbing rising costs for months. The Rs 8 increase is huge,” said Prashanth Raj, director of IDC. “We may be forced to increase prices by at least Rs 5. A revision is inevitable.”
Bangalore Hotels Association said Thursday the hike would significantly impact hotels, restaurants, bakeries and sweet shops, where milk consumption is far higher than in households. PC Rao, honorary president of the association, urged govt to reconsider the decision.
The association said affordable hotels and darshinis cater largely to daily-wage workers, lower-income groups and the middle class, and any increase would be passed on to consumers. Several darshini owners told 
TOI that discussions on price revision have already started.
Anger boils overTejas PB, regular consumer:  A hike of this scale is unimaginable, especially at a time when the job market is struggling and household budgets are already under pressure. For many drivers, daily-wage workers and professionals, a cup of tea or coffee is an affordable source of energy during long working hours. When even a tea-and-bun combination becomes expensive, it will hit the middle class and lower-income groups the hardest
Amritha, assistant professor, St Joseph’s University: Though this will strain household budgets, consumers may yet accept hikes if they are assured of quality and if standards are met. Any revision should ensure farmers receive better incentives and fair returns
Samhitha V, advocate: People will stop consuming coffee or tea, but essential commodities must remain affordable. No one should think twice before buying milk. For many professions, including mine, meeting over a cup of tea or coffee is part of everyday life. The state govt should review its decision
Maruthi, private employee: I regularly take milk and other dairy products such as paneer as part of my fitness routine. Salaries and annual increments are not keeping pace with the rising cost of living. This decision alone could increase my monthly spending by around Rs 500. Govt should take a more comprehensive view of how such price hikes affect ordinary citizens before making these decisions

stories.headline: Food Safety officials conduct State-wide inspection at 45 packaged drinking water units; notices issued to 24
stories.deck: 32 water samples sent for testing; misbranded water seized in Mysuru and Davangere; a unit in Mulbagal shut down
stories.bodyText:
The Food Safety and Drug Administration Department conducted a special State-wide inspection of 45 packaged drinking water units on Thursday.
Several violations, including unhygienic conditions, absence of medical fitness certificates for staff, missing licences from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), labelling defects and failure to produce pest control certificates, were found during the inspection.
As many as 32 water samples have been sent to government food laboratories for testing, while notices have been issued to 24 units for the violations.
Misbranded packaged drinking water was seized from units in Mysuru and Davangere. A unit at Mulbagal in Kolar district was shut down due to unhygienic conditions.

stories.headline: Bengaluru woman dies a month after crash as GBA-traffic police coordination comes under scrutiny
stories.bodyText:
A 57-year-old woman succumbed to her injuries on Wednesday after battling for her life for a month following a collision with a minibus on HMT Main Road in north Bengaluru.
The incident has raised questions about coordination between the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) and the Greater Bengaluru Authority’s (GBA) new corporations, as the accident spot required a speed breaker and residents had written to officials much earlier, highlighting vulnerable stretches of the road.
The deceased has been identified as Vijayalakshmi, a resident of HMT Quarters in the same area. On September 30, she was crossing HMT Main Road, which connects to NASIN Circle, when a minibus hit her. CCTV footage of the accident shows her being flung into the air before suffering a grievous fall that left her with multiple injuries, including a head injury. She succumbed to her injuries on October 28.
Deepali J., a resident of the same locality, told The Hindu that they had written to the local traffic police station well before the crash, warning that the spot was vulnerable to accidents. “The vehicles on the stretch move at high speed and at least near the crossroads; there is a need for speed breakers,” she said.
Missing coordination
According to BTP sources, soon after the crash, they identified a pattern that revealed that the stretch had witnessed nearly seven accidents in a period of over a year. BTP sources said they had sent a letter to the GBA, while corporation officials said they had not received any such request.
Typically, the BTP identifies vulnerable spots and requirements such as lane markings, footpath bollards, and other pedestrian infrastructure. Under the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), the Traffic Engineering Cell (TEC) used to coordinate with the BTP and initiate the necessary works.
A senior police officer said that, under the new GBA setup, the police send proposals to the Traffic Management Centre (TMC), which forwards them to the GBA. The proposals are then sent to the respective corporations. However, the hierarchical movement of files leads to delays, even though such minor works require coordination among officers at the ground level.
A senior GBA official told The Hindu that the new corporations also have TECs, but they are primarily focusing on skywalks, while the general section oversees lane markings and speed breakers. The official acknowledged that a shortage of assistant executive engineers across the corporations had hampered the pace of some work, as multiple responsibilities are being assigned to junior engineers.
Need for audit
Bengaluru has about 66 accident blackspots, according to BTP sources. While even these spots are awaiting fixes, several traffic pattern monitoring volunteers point out that residential roads have also become accident-prone, warranting an audit.
Prasanna Bhat, a traffic volunteer, said accidents had become increasingly common on residential roads where two roads intersect perpendicularly. “There is a dire need for an audit of such stretches by either the BTP or the civic body. The problem may appear smaller, but there have been multiple minor accidents in the past,” he stressed

briefs.headline: Bengaluru finds its harmony in group singing and choir
briefs.bodyText:
This weekend, you don’t have to be a pro in singing to find your voice in a choir. At Flash Jams, a one-day choir pop-up in Bengaluru, people come together to sing familiar songs, experiment with vocal harmonies and make music as a community. For Danish Abdi, the Choir Director, the idea grew from a desire to recreate the camaraderie of college music sessions. “I wanted to keep it the same way – a very living-room, friends-jamming kind of experience at Flash Jams,” he shares. The format began with small sessions among friends and grew into larger events across India.
‘Community comes before the music’
For Danish, the appeal goes beyond learning the technicalities of music. The sessions offer people a chance to unwind, meet others who share their interests and spend time away from their phones. “Community is actually the first draw of a Flash Jam,” he says. Participants come together to sing their favourite songs, meet fellow music lovers and find a sense of belonging. While some are curious about how harmonies work, others simply enjoy singing familiar tunes in a group. “It’s always community first and then the harmony aspect,” Danish says.
‘A space where every voice belongs’
At a session, participants begin with icebreakers and simple exercises that introduce them to vocal harmony. They are then grouped according to their vocal ranges and taught different parts of a familiar song. As the individual parts come together, participants hear how multiple voices can add depth to a melody they already know. Danish says the sessions are designed to be low-pressure. Those who feel shy can sit back, listen and join in when they feel ready. “The aim is not to turn participants into skilled harmony singers in a couple of hours, but to help them experience the joy of singing together,” he adds.

briefs.headline: Karnataka govt proposes strict rules for coaching centres; no children under 15, classes only for five hours, and mental health counsellor on campus
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 In what could be a major crackdown on high-pressure coaching centres, Karnataka govt has issued draft rules barring children under the age of 15 from enrolling in private coaching institutes and restricting daily tutorial operations to fixed hours between 6am and 9pm.
The proposed Karnataka Tutorial Institutions or Coaching Centre (Registration and Regulation) Rules, 2026, notified by the higher education department Wednesday, aim to curb rising academic stress, misleading advertisements, and non-refundable fee traps.
Under the draft norms, private coaching centres are strictly prohibited from admitting students who are below 15 years of age or who have not completed their secondary school (class 10) exams. To prevent exhaustion and mental pressure among young learners, the state has capped total daily coaching — inclusive of tests, revision, and doubt-clearing sessions — to a maximum of five hours. “The time of operation of the tutorial institutions shall be between 6am and 9pm,” the official notification states, adding that classes cannot be scheduled at unreasonably early or late hours.
Furthermore, institutes cannot conduct classes during regular school or college hours, to prevent nominal attendance in mainstream schools. 
Currently, many coaching centres follow a model where students join dummy PU colleges and spend most of their days at the coaching centres.
The draft also mandates that coaching centres have a mental health counsellor and conduct periodic workshops and sensitisation sessions regarding mental health for students and parents.
Coaching centres also cannot make public the results of assessment tests, either within or beyond their premises. “Keeping assessment tests confidential, they should be used for regular analysis of student performance... and the student whose performance is deteriorating should be provided counselling as per the provisions of these guidelines,” the draft states.
Tutors will have to undergo training in mental health issues to convey information effectively and sensitively to students about areas of improvement. Apart from options for admission in engineering and medical institutes, “information about other career options should be provided to students” so they do not feel stressed about their future and can explore alternative careers.
Coaching centres are also prohibited from employing faculty from govt or aided institutions. They cannot hire the services of tutors convicted of any offence involving moral turpitude.
There will be two district-level monitoring committees — one for Bengaluru Urban district and another for the remaining districts of the state — to monitor the functioning of these centres and oversee compliance.
This draft will replace the Karnataka Tutorial Institutions (Registration & Regulation) Rules, 2001. Members of the public can send recommendations within 15 days of publication of the draft.
What’s being streamlined?
Coaching centre in the draft refers to “a centre, established, run, or administered by any person to provide coaching for any study programme or competitive exams or academic support... for more than 20 students.”
Meanwhile, tutorial institution means “an establishment that provides academic support, acting as a personalised learning environment (includes coaching centre or tutorials or tuition classes or trust or society or institution or any other such establishment) that supplements mainstream education, focusing on exam preparation, clarification, and individual progress of students.”
Both are synonymous in the draft.
On fees & refunds
Addressing long-standing complaints from parents regarding exorbitant advance payments, the new regulations mandate that coaching centres cannot collect the entire course fee in a single upfront lump sum. Instead, they must offer parents the option to pay in at least four equal instalments.
The tuition fees should be fair and reasonable, and receipts should be made available.
In addition, the rules introduce an easy exit policy: if a student drops out or withdraws early, the institution must refund the advance fee for the remaining duration on a pro-rata basis within 10 days. Hostel and mess fees must also be refunded promptly.
On registration
* Tutorial institution has to register through the Seva Sindhu portal in whose jurisdiction it is situated
* Every application is to be accompanied by geotagged location of the premises
* In case of multiple branches, each branch will be treated as a separate tutorial institution
* If there are hostel facilities, all necessary approvals should be taken
* If operating under a franchise agreement, the application for registration should be submitted by the franchisor on behalf of the franchisee
* Registration fee of Rs 15,000 + Rs 5,000 for each course
* Deputy commissioner of each district will be the registering authority. Commissioner, department of collegiate and technical education, will be the appellate authority
* Validity of registration is 3 years
No false promises
The draft regulations strictly ban coaching centres from making misleading promises, guaranteeing top ranks, or publishing deceptive claims regarding student results and faculty qualifications.
Required infra
* Assign at least 1sqm of floor space per student in classrooms and 10sqm for teacher to move around
* Adopt standard measures for disaster risk reduction
* Adhere to fire safety codes, building safety codes and other standards. Fire safety 12 certificate, building safety certificate and sanitation certificate to be obtained
* The centre should be fully electrified and adequately ventilated, with provision for sufficient illumination in each classroom
* Separate toilets for boys and girls
* CCTV coverage
* Complaint box
* Extracurricular activities
* Minimum of 20 and maximum of 80 students per class
Penalty
Unregistered centres operating within six months face immediate sealing by authorities. The appellate authority has the power to cancel registrations or slap heavy penalties of up to Rs 5 lakh for serious non-compliance.

briefs.headline: Fresh bids undercut earlier rates as Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd defends waste contracts in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Even as the city’s revamped door-to-door waste collection rollout suffered a setback after several contractors declined to accept work orders, fresh bids received by Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Ltd (BSWML) for some of the re-tendered packages have come in at premiums significantly lower than the 14% originally approved by govt.
The agency had been forced to re-tender multiple packages after contractors, who had secured the deals, argued that the 14% premium over the estimated contract value was inadequate.
According to BSWML, re-tendered package 7 (Gandhinagar) attracted a premium of close to 4.5%, package 9 (Rajajinagar) 7%, package 10 (Malleswaram) 9% and package 19 (Bommanahalli) 9.8%. All four packages had earlier been approved at a premium of around 14%. BSWML CEO Kare Gowda said the fresh bids undermine the argument that the approved premium was insufficient. “If premium was the main problem, why would new bidders quote less than 10%? Once govt approval is obtained and work orders are not accepted, it results in a huge loss of time and delays rollout of services,” he told 
TOI
.
Officials said lower premiums would result in savings for the agency while enabling implementation of the new waste collection model. Another senior BSWML official said the refusal to accept certain work orders appeared to stem more from contractors’ internal issues than concerns over the premium itself.
The waste management overhaul, covering 33 city packages, has faced repeated delays, prompting the agency to re-tender several contracts and restart parts of the procurement process.

briefs.headline: IKEA to open second store in Bengaluru, this time in the south
briefs.deck: Spanning over 80,000 sq. ft. (7,783 sq. m.), the store is located not far from Konanakunte Cross Metro Station
briefs.bodyText:
IKEA India, the Indian arm of the Swedish furniture and home furnishing retailer, is set to open its second store in Bengaluru on November 5 at Purva Zentech on Kanakapura Main Road. The conglomerate’s second store in the city, targeting potential customers from south Bengaluru and neighbouring areas, comes around four years after it opened its first store in the city, at Nagasandra, in 2022.
Spanning over 80,000 sq. ft. (7,783 sq. m.), the store is located near Konanakunte Cross Namma Metro station.
The store offers more than 5,200 products for customers to explore, with over 3,000 available for immediate takeaway. The complete IKEA range of over 7,000 products can be ordered in-store or through the IKEA website, app, and Shop by Phone service. Customers can also take a break from shopping and enjoy Swedish favourites and local treats at the 100-seater IKEA Restaurant.
Journey in Bengaluru
IKEA began its journey in Bengaluru with e-commerce in 2021. According to the company, IKEA reaches over 300 million visitors across India through its online and offline channels, and has a community of more than 3 million IKEA Family members.
“Bengaluru holds a special place in our India journey. Over the last five years, we have been welcomed into thousands of homes and have had the opportunity to learn from customers about how they live, what they value, and how their needs are evolving. These insights have been instrumental in designing our new south Bengaluru store. Opening our second store in the city is a proud milestone and reflects our commitment to being more accessible and convenient,” said Patrik Antoni, CEO, IKEA India.
At present, IKEA has stores in seven cities in India — Hyderabad, Navi Mumbai, Worli in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, and Pune.
In September, Mr. Antoni had met Karnataka’s Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to discuss new stores, local sourcing, and developing a wider vendor base in the State.
He invited Mr. Shivakumar to inaugurate IKEA’s upcoming second at Konanakunte Cross. The Swedish retailer is expanding its physical footprint in India while simultaneously ramping up its online reach. IKEA is broadening its presence beyond its traditional large-format stores. The company recently expanded its presence in Delhi-NCR with a new 30,000 square feet store, while it has also been relying on smaller formats and e-commerce to reach more customers.
One idea, multiple formats
On April 30, 2025, IKEA unveiled its first ‘Plan and Order Point’ (PaOP) in India at the Essensai 067 Experience Centre on Whitefield-Hoskote Road in Bengaluru. The 740 square metre space is nowhere comparable in size to the flagship store at Nagasandra, but serves the retailer’s aim to expand — both in format as well as geographically — to serve bustling east Bengaluru.
The new format, according to IKEA, serves as a dedicated customer meeting point, bringing expert home design knowledge closer to customers with personalised consultations, flexible planning support, and seamless installation services.
Pooja Grover, Country Expansion Manager, IKEA India, said, “Bengaluru, by 2030, is expected to have a home furnishing potential of about ₹216 billion. It’s a huge growth market, along with Delhi. And it’s one of our priority markets, so we are exploring to have quite a few of stores in various formats here. Why east of Bengaluru? It’s the IT hub, and because of that, you have a lot of young professionals here who are well-travelled, diverse, and from all over the country. If you do a mapping of the residential hotspots, you can see there’s huge amounts of residential catchments being added in the east along Hosakote and Sarjapur and these areas.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka IT union objects to Union Minister Piyush Goyal’s pitch that Indians are willing to work beyond office hours
briefs.deck: KITU claimed that such remarks effectively give corporations a free hand to disregard working hour regulations and weekly holidays
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka State IT/ITeS Employees Union (KITU) has condemned the remarks by Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal at the India-Netherlands Business Forum, where he pitched India as a great investment destination, saying, “Nobody in India will tell you it’s 5 o’clock. And certainly, no Indian will ever remind you it’s the weekend.”
KITU claimed that such remarks effectively give corporations a free hand to disregard working hour regulations, weekly holidays, and safeguards in labour laws.
“By projecting that Indian workers will remain available to employers at all hours, including weekends, the Minister is promoting a culture of chattel slavery,” the union remarked, while also equating the Minister’s comments to similar remarks previously made by Infosys co-founder Narayana Murthy and the L&T Chairperson S. N. Subrahmanyan, who advocated long working hours.
On October 26, Mr. Goyal tried to pitch the ‘hardworking nature of Indians’ to European business leaders. “Nobody in India will tell you it is 5 o’clock. And certainly, no Indian will ever remind you it is the weekend. And that is what I bring to the table. Economies of scale, for your business to grow into a dimension you probably can never even imagine. Because everything in India is to scale.”
KITU pointed out that such relentless glorification of overwork places corporate profits above workers’ dignity, health, and fundamental rights, and that Indian workers are already facing extended working hours, workplace stress, burnout, and the erosion of personal and family life.
“Time for rest, family, social participation, and personal development is not a privilege granted by employers; it is an essential part of a dignified human life. The normalisation of brutal and inhumane labour extraction, and disregard for labour protections by a Union Minister are unacceptable. Instead of echoing corporate interests, the government must uphold workers’ rights and ensure the effective enforcement of labour laws and international labour standards,” demanded Suhas Adiga, General Secretary at KITU.
While politicians such as Karti Chidambaram from the opposition have criticised the Minister’s remarks, industrialists and entrepreneurs, including Harsh Goenka and Ashneer Grover, defended Mr. Goyal’s position.

stories.headline: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears; Brent nears $116
stories.deck: Crude oil prices are increasing as Brent crude surpasses $115 per barrel amid escalating tensions. Attacks by Yemen’s Houthi group on Saudi oil sites raise fears of supply disruptions. Efforts for diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain unyielding, contributing to market uncertainty. Meanwhile, Iranian reports of maritime incidents further heighten security concerns in the…
stories.bodyText:
Crude oil prices continued their upward march on Friday, with Brent crossing $115 a barrel as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf heightened fears of supply disruptions. The benchmarks were also heading for their fourth consecutive monthly rise, with US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April.
Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $115.74 a barrel by 0122 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 72 cents, or 0.71 per cent, to $102.72.
Brent was on course for a nearly 14 per cent gain in October, while WTI was set to jump around 15 per cent. Both were heading for their sharpest monthly increases since July.
The latest escalation came on Thursday, when Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed attacks on key Saudi oil installations, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately reported intercepting a cruise missile launched towards the kingdom’s western region.
The developments have heightened concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and shipping routes at a time when prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough remain uncertain.
“Continued kinetic action around the Strait of Hormuz amidst doubts of a viable diplomatic pathway are keeping oil prices elevated in expectation of an escalation of the conflict in coming weeks,” said Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Marquee.
The Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of concern for energy markets, with any disruption to traffic through the waterway threatening to constrain global oil supplies.
Peace overtures fail to ease tensions
Efforts to reopen diplomatic channels between Washington and Tehran have yet to provide markets with reassurance.
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had contacted Iran to help it obtain medical supplies. This followed US media reports that Vance had written to Iran’s top security official in a bid to restart peace negotiations.
Iran has received the letter but has not responded, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported. Tehran is insisting that Washington accept its conditions, the agency said, quoting the Iranian position that “any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable.”
At sea, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reported that three tankers had hit sea mines, exploded and caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The report added to the security concerns surrounding maritime traffic in the region.
The heightened risks are also prompting changes to corporate travel plans. ExxonMobil and Chevron have cancelled plans for their executives to attend the United Arab Emirates’ biggest oil show next week, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.
With crude prices already recording substantial monthly gains, traders are watching for signs that the conflict could further disrupt oil production or transportation. The trajectory of diplomatic efforts and the security of key energy routes are likely to remain central to market sentiment.

stories.headline: Cognizant cuts Project Leap cost estimate to $180–250 million; headcount rises
stories.deck: IT services firm reports 10,100 more employees year-on-year; quarterly employee separation costs stood at $46 million; CEO says over 50% of its code is AI-assisted
stories.bodyText:
Cognizant Technology Solutions has lowered its estimated costs for Project Leap, a restructuring programme that includes employee severance, even as its total headcount rose by 10,100 over the past year.
The company had previously estimated Project Leap costs at $230 million to $320 million, with substantially all the costs expected to be incurred in 2026, according to its second-quarter 2026 results. The revised estimate of $180 million to $250 million was disclosed in its third-quarter earnings, released on October 29.
Total headcount stood at 359,900 as of September 30, up 3,200 from June 30 and 10,100 from September 30, 2025, the company said.
Introduced earlier this year, Project Leap is designed to accelerate Cognizant’s transition to “the operating model of the future” by funding investments in integrated offerings, AI capabilities and partnerships, reshaping productivity through competitive offerings and upskilling its workforce. The programme also involves workforce restructuring, with employee severance and other personnel-related costs accounting for a substantial share of its estimated expenditure.
Cognizant expects to incur $140 million to $160 million of the revised costs in 2026, with the remainder expected through the first quarter of 2027. The estimate includes $150 million to $200 million in employee severance and other personnel-related costs, and $30 million to $50 million in other charges. The company did not disclose how many employees would be affected or in which countries.
In the third quarter, Cognizant recorded $51 million in Project Leap charges, including $46 million in employee separation costs. Charges for the first nine months of 2026 totalled $135 million, of which $102 million was related to employee separation.
Cognizant expects Project Leap to generate about $200 million in savings in 2026, which it says will be used primarily to fund investments in integrated offerings, AI capabilities and partnerships.
The company reported third-quarter revenue of $5.664 billion, up 4.6% year-on-year and 4.8% in constant currency. Net income rose to $627 million from $274 million a year earlier, when it was affected by a one-time, non-cash tax expense of $390 million related to the enactment of the U.S. One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Adjusted net income edged down to $670 million from $675 million.
Cognizant’s GAAP operating margin fell 60 basis points year-on-year to 15.4%, while its adjusted operating margin rose 30 basis points to 16.3%. The company excludes Project Leap charges from its adjusted operating margin.
Chief Executive Ravi Kumar S. said in the earnings release that “over 50% of our code” is now AI-assisted and that its associates have earned more than 95,000 frontier AI badges and certifications. He also cited continued improvement in revenue and adjusted operating income per employee.
Chief Financial Officer Jatin Dalal said the company achieved its third-quarter results while investing in strategic partnerships and AI skilling initiatives and integrating recently completed acquisitions.

stories.headline: September pain for credit card companies: Spending down 6% at Rs 2L cr
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Credit card spending fell 5.9% year-on-year to about Rs 2 lakh crore in Sept 2026, the first annual decline since Feb 2021, as festive purchases shifted to Oct and a high base amplified the fall.
Spending had risen 13.3% month-on-month in Sept 2025 after GST rate cuts took effect and online festive sales began in the last week of the month. Spending in Aug and Sept combined was broadly flat, declining 0.4% year-on-year, suggesting the shift in festive sales accounted for much of Sept’s fall. CareEdge expects spending to rise to Rs 2.3-2.4 lakh crore in Oct on account of festive sales.
According to an analysis of RBI data by CareEdge Ratings, growth had already slowed to 6.7% year-on-year in July and Aug from 7.9% in Q1FY27. Credit card spending rose 4.9% in H1FY27 to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, with growth slowing to 2.1% in Q2 from 7.9% in Q1, largely because of Sept’s decline.
Spending fell 9.3% year-on-year at public sector banks (PSBs) and 6.2% at private sector banks (PVBs), while foreign banks recorded 9.2% growth and small finance banks 92.4%, albeit on a small base. Large issuers also attributed weaker annual growth to the shift in the festive season from Sept to Oct.
The number of outstanding credit cards rose 10.5% year-on-year to 12.5 crore in Sept, the fastest growth since Nov 2024. Banks added 12.6 lakh cards during the month, against about 12 lakh in Aug. In Q2FY27, the largest private bank issued 1.4 million cards, up 19% from Q1, while SBI Card added more than 1.1 million accounts, up 18% from a year earlier.
Banks remain keen to expand retail lending, with bankers reporting stronger demand for retail and personal loans and some easing in lending terms. They expect demand to remain strong in Q3FY27, supporting card issuance through the festive quarter.
Spending per card fell 14.8% year-on-year to Rs 16,305 in Sept, extending its annual decline to three consecutive months as spending weakened while the card base expanded. The fall was amplified by a 12.2% month-on-month increase in spending per card in Sept 2025. Cardholders made 61 crore transactions during the month, up 23.2% year-on-year, with each card used around 4.9 times against 4.4 times a year earlier. Transactions fell 3.5% month-on-month, while daily volumes were broadly unchanged.
The average transaction value fell 23.6% year-on-year to Rs 3,343, although it rose from Rs 3,201 in Aug. The decline was sharper for online payments, at 28%, than for point-of-sale (PoS) transactions, at 13%. The high base from festive purchases made online in Sept 2025 and the growing use of UPI for card payments, which generally involve smaller amounts, explain the decline. SBI Card reported UPI-linked spending of Rs 21,300 crore in Q2FY27, around a fifth of its total spending.

stories.headline: Yulu forays into Nashik for EV-powered deliveries
stories.deck: Nashik is Yulu’s second market in Maharashtra after Mumbai, where its hyperlocal EV ecosystem has helped delivery persons with affordable green rides
stories.bodyText:
Yulu, the electric mobility-as-a-service (e-MaaS) platform, has launched its service in Nashik under its Yulu Business Partner (YBP) vertical in partnership with Approach Auto Mobility, a venture led by entrepreneur Jai Dhanani.
Nashik is Yulu’s second market in Maharashtra after Mumbai, where its hyperlocal EV ecosystem has helped delivery persons with affordable green rides over the past seven years.
Steeped in history and spirituality, Nashik is rapidly expanding its digital economy. It has more than 25 operational dark stores and 1,500 high-volume restaurants, and city-wide deliveries have doubled over the past year to about 25,000 deliveries a day, according to Yulu.
This demand is expected to accelerate as more consumers embrace the convenience of the on-demand economy. Yet, most doorstep orders are powered by petrol vehicles, leaving delivery partners burdened with high vehicle EMIs and recurring fuel and maintenance costs, it said.
“This is the market gap that Yulu is addressing with its technology-powered and high-uptime mobility platform,” it added.
Operations will begin with a fleet of 100 DeX EVs based out of a Yulu Centre in Rajiv Nagar. The service will cover Nashik city and expand into surrounding areas as demand grows.
Amit Gupta, co-founder & CEO, Yulu, said, “India’s next phase of e-mobility adoption will be shaped by non-metro cities where changing consumer expectations and the expansion of quick commerce are reshaping urban logistics. The depth of demand for sustainable, reliable, and accessible solutions from both consumers and delivery partners in Nashik makes it the perfect time for a hyperlocal goods mobility platform like Yulu to launch its service in the city.”
Jai Dhanani, founder, Approach Auto Mobility, said, “As an existing battery swapping franchise partner of Yuma Energy, we were already familiar with the Yulu Group’s purpose-built system and technology-driven approach to mobility.”
“The latest partnership gets us closer to our aim of making EV-powered deliveries the default in Nashik — a goal we will achieve by offering delivery partners a lower cost per kilometre and near-zero downtime network, even as we simultaneously help brands unlock a dependable and low-emission fleet that grows with them as a partner,” he said.
With the launch in Nashik, Yulu extends its overall presence to 13 cities, including the four metro markets it operates directly: Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, and Hyderabad.

briefs.headline: B.R. Shetty moves Bombay High Court seeking directions against Bank of Baroda in NMC Healthcare case
briefs.deck: The underlying suit seeks $15 billion from all defendants jointly and severally, with interest at 18% annually.
briefs.bodyText:
Bavaguthu Raghuram (B.R.) Shetty, founder and promoter of the failed UAE-based healthcare venture NMC Healthcare and UAE Exchange, has moved the Bombay High Court seeking protection for his $15 billion damages claim against Bank of Baroda (BoB). In two interim applications, he has sought security for the claim and preservation of the bank’s electronic records and documents relating to its $600 million settlement in the NMC dispute.
Through his applications, filed by his constituted attorney Shishir Shetty, he has sought three levels of protection pending final disposal of the suit: security for the claim, earmarking of funds through a specific provision or non-distributable reserve, or disclosure of the claim as a contingent liability in the bank’s balance sheet. He has also sought compliance affidavits and ad-interim relief on the same terms.
The underlying suit seeks $15 billion from all defendants jointly and severally, with interest at 18% annually. The claim comprises $5 billion each for direct damages arising from alleged fraud and negligence, consequential damages including loss of opportunity, and loss of reputation and goodwill, the last being claimed against BoB alone.
The applications cite the bank’s disclosures between May and July 2026. According to Mr. Shetty, BoB’s FY26 annual report stated that it had a good case in proceedings initiated by the joint administrators of NMC companies before the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Courts, without making a provision or disclosing a contingent liability.
Within weeks, the bank agreed to settle the proceedings for about $600 million (₹5,700 crore). On July 2, it disclosed the settlement under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) Regulations, stating that it was “without admission of liability”. The application alleges that BoB’s shares fell sharply following the development and that the settlement terms remain undisclosed.
Mr. Shetty alleges that after he relinquished control of the group around 2012 and stepped down as CEO in March 2017, the Manghat brothers and their associates drained the NMC companies, with BoB, the group’s principal banker until around 2019, allegedly serving as the instrument.
The application argues that the absence of a provision could impede enforcement of any decree, with the bank potentially citing risks to depositors, capital adequacy and regulatory standing. It seeks an urgent hearing ahead of BoB’s results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.
In the second application, Mr. Shetty seeks appointment of a court commissioner, assisted by an independent forensic expert, to image the bank’s electronic records and prevent their loss or alteration.
Represented by Waseem Pangarkar of MZM Legal LLP, Mr. Shetty has yet to establish his allegations in court.
Bank not been served with the interim applications: BoB
In an exchange filing Bank of Baroda said, “As the Bank clarified in its earlier filing with the stock exchanges on 14 October 2026, the Bank has not been served with such a suit. The Bank has also not been served with the interim applications that were subject of today’s press inquiries.”
“In both cases, the Bank maintains that it cannot comment on the contents of pleadings or interim applications that it has not been served with and that have not been heard before the court,” it said.
“As a matter of principle, it would be improper for the Bank to respond to untested allegations in relation to court proceedings in public media. It appears from the website of the Hon’ble Bombay High Court that both the suit and the interim applications filed by Dr. Shetty are either yet to be scrutinised or registered by the Hon’ble Bombay High Court. As such, the allegations remain untested until such time that a Court considers them in accordance with law,” it said.
“Contents of the suit and interim applications appear to have been selectively disseminated to the news media on the eve of the announcement of the Bank’s quarterly results with an improper intention. The Bank will take appropriate steps in relation to such dissemination,” it added.

stories.headline: 'I was very happy': Mandhana reveals Dhoni's special message after World Cup win

India's women's team achieved their first ODI World Cup title by defeating South Africa on…
stories.bodyText:
Smriti Mandhana
 has revealed that former India captain 
MS Dhoni
 personally congratulated her after the Indian women's team lifted their maiden ODI World Cup title in November 2025.
Speaking at an event featuring 
Dhoni
, Mandhana recalled receiving a WhatsApp message from the legendary cricketer following India's historic triumph. She admitted that the gesture made her particularly happy, knowing that Dhoni is not someone who uses his phone frequently.
“He actually did send me a message after the World Cup win. I know he does not use his phone a lot. I was very happy that he used WhatsApp to congratulate all of us," Mandhana said.
Host Harsha Bhogle then asked Mandhana whether she had saved Dhoni's number.
“I did have his number," she replied.
Dhoni, meanwhile, offered an interesting explanation for choosing Mandhana as the recipient of his message. He revealed that she was the only member of the Indian women's team whose contact number he had saved.
“I did not know anyone else’s (number) from the team. I wanted the message to go through. We had just shot (a commercial) before that. I thought, ‘Let me send a message to Smriti’ and I mentioned, ‘Please wish everyone who is part of the team," Dhoni said.
India created history on November 2, 2025, defeating South Africa by 52 runs in Navi Mumbai to win their first-ever Women's ODI World Cup. 
The triumph ended the team's long wait for an ICC title.
Batting first in the final, India posted 298/7, with Shafali Verma leading the charge with 87 runs and Deepti Sharma contributing 58. Deepti then delivered with the ball, taking five wickets as South Africa were dismissed for 246 despite a century from Laura Wolvaardt.

stories.headline: Azmatullah Omarzai scripts history after walking in at 5/4, smashes T20I world record
stories.deck: In a dazzling comeback, Azmatullah Omarzai rescued Afghanistan with an extraordinary century, scoring 116 runs from 50 deliveries after a shaky start against Zimbabwe. This achievement marked a record for T20I lower-order batters. His pivotal collaboration with Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, worth 142 runs for the sixth wicket, pushed Afghanistan to a total of 221/7. Although Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza…
stories.bodyText:
Azmatullah Omarzai produced a stunning rescue act with the bat, smashing a record-breaking century to help Afghanistan recover from a disastrous start and post 221/7 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Walking in with Afghanistan reeling at 5/4, Omarzai launched a counter-attack that completely changed the course of the innings. He hammered 116 off just 50 balls, striking five fours and 12 sixes at an astonishing strike rate of 232.
With the effort, Omarzai registered the highest individual score by a batter coming in at No. 6 or lower in T20Is involving Full Member nations. He went past the previous record of 89, scored by former Afghanistan captain Mohammad Nabi against Ireland in 2017.
The record-breaking knock also put Omarzai ahead of Sam Billings (87 against West Indies in 2019), Cameron White (85 not out against Sri Lanka in 2010) and David Miller (85 not out against Pakistan in 2021) on the list.
Afghanistan's innings had been in complete disarray after Zimbabwe's bowlers reduced them to 5/4. Several top-order batters departed cheaply, while Sediqullah Atal managed just 17 off 21 deliveries before falling in the ninth over.
Omarzai found an ideal partner in Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai, and the duo launched a remarkable recovery. They added 142 runs off only 59 balls for the sixth wicket, with Ijaz contributing a blistering 52 off 27 deliveries, including five fours and three sixes.
The partnership was finally broken when Ijaz fell with the score at 180. Omarzai continued his assault before being dismissed in the 19th over, having already produced one of the finest rescue acts in Afghanistan's T20I history.
Captain Rashid Khan provided a spectacular finish, smashing an unbeaten 25 off just six balls, including four sixes. Mujeeb Ur Rahman remained not out on two as Afghanistan closed their innings at 221/7, scoring at 11.05 runs per over.
Rashid also achieved a major milestone during the match, becoming the first bowler to claim 200 wickets in T20Is.
Zimbabwe fall short despite Sikandar Raza's century
Zimbabwe were unable to overcome the imposing target despite a determined effort from captain Sikandar Raza, who scored his second T20I century.
Raza fought till the end, but the visitors ultimately fell short, with Afghanistan's early batting collapse proving to be a distant memory after Omarzai's extraordinary intervention.
Tafadzwa Tsiga offered valuable support on his debut, while the dismissal of Ryan Burl dealt another blow to Zimbabwe's hopes.
The victory also extended Afghanistan's remarkable dominance in the rivalry, marking their eighth consecutive T20I series win against Zimbabwe. The visitors are yet to win a T20I series against Afghanistan.

stories.headline: Kotian caps a career-best haul to set up Mumbai’s win
stories.deck: Kotian claimed eight for 84 to finish with a match haul of 11 wickets as Haryana was bowled out for 256 at the stroke of tea
stories.bodyText:
Tanush Kotian spun his web around Haryana with career-best figures to set up Mumbai’s third consecutive Ranji Trophy victory, with a bonus point, as the hosts continued their march towards regaining the title at the Sharad Pawar Academy ground on Thursday (October 29, 2026).
Kotian claimed eight for 84 to finish with a match haul of 11 wickets as Haryana was bowled out for 256 at the stroke of tea. Mumbai’s openers, Divyaansh Saxena (30 not out, 25b, 2x4, 2x6) and Angkrish Raghuvanshi (67 not out, 39b, 7x4, 3x6), then made light work of the 97-run target, overhauling it in less than 11 overs.
When Kotian opened the bowling from the pavilion end in the morning, Mumbai needed eight wickets to seal victory, while Haryana had to bat out of its skin to salvage a draw. The off-spinner wasted little time in making an impact, inducing an edge from Yashvardhan Dalal that Sarfaraz Khan pouched safely.
Himanshu Rana, who had retired hurt after being struck on the helmet the previous evening, returned to join the resolute Nishant Sindhu. But Kotian struck again close to lunch, getting one to turn sharply into Rana, whose edge was safely held by Saxena at leg-slip. Sindhu then fell at the stroke of lunch, inside-edging an audacious sweep that wicketkeeper Akash Anand caught cleanly.
Kotian continued to vary his angles cleverly, but Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral resisted for nearly two hours. The breakthrough finally came when Kotian, bowling over the wicket, turned one through Thakral’s defence to hit the stumps. The resistance unravelled thereafter, allowing Kotian to register his career-best in an innings and a match.
Mumbai’s openers ensured there was no late drama. Unleashing their T20 strokes against Haryana’s spinners, they cleared the boundary with ease. Raghuvanshi even employed the reverse-sweep effectively against left-arm spinner Sindhu before sealing the win with a swat over midwicket for six off off-spinner Kanishk Chouhan.

briefs.headline: Roman Reigns inspired his punches, Russell gave him a nickname: Meet Kapil Pokhariya
briefs.deck: Inspired by WWE star Roman Reigns and nicknamed ‘Khatima ka Russell’ for his big-hitting prowess, Indian Army havaldar Kapil Pokhariya took an unconventional route to boxing. Growing up in a small Uttarakhand village, he went from punching homemade bags filled with mountain soil to winning bronze in the men’s 90kg category at the 2026 Asian Games. Kapil reflects on his childhood, his father’s…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Jumping on cotton-filled mattresses, punching pillows, throwing them over walls and hitting a homemade punching bag filled with mountain soil - Kapil Pokhariya’s childhood was all about pro-wrestling.
His fascination with pro-wrestler 
Roman Reigns
 was well known in his locality. He would skip meals, playtime, and outings to watch WWE programming on television. Once the show was over, he would try to copy the moves and punches at home.
Little did he know that this childhood fascination could one day bring him his biggest recognition.
Today, Kapil - an 
Indian Army
 havaldar - is an 
Asian Games
 medallist. Kapil won bronze in the men’s 90kg boxing event at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
“I never knew that copying Roman Reigns and practising those punches would bring me this far. I used to save recordings of his videos, and I still have them. I am really proud of where I am today. Honestly, I started learning how to throw punches by copying Roman Reigns (laugh),” Kapil told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.
"My favourite was WrestleMania and Money in the Bank," he said.
From Khatima to the Asian Games podium
Kapil hails from Chakarpur village in Khatima, Uttarakhand, far from the major boxing centres that have produced several Indian stars.
His father, Narendra Singh Pokhariya, served in the Indian Army. He wanted his son to study well and join the Army as a commissioned officer. Boxing, however, was never part of the original plan.
Kapil Pokhariya with his father (Image credit: Special arrangement)
Narendra often watched his son copy WWE stars at home. Initially, he would scold and even beat him for damaging things around the house. But his view slowly changed when he saw Kapil putting sand into a thick sack after returning from school and punching it with all his strength.
“A teacher used to teach boxing at a nearby school. I saw the students punching a bag and decided to make one myself. My father scolded me in the beginning, but later he took me to a training centre and got me admitted there. That is how I got into boxing,” Kapil said.
From a small training ground to the boxing ring
Kapil did not begin his boxing journey at a big academy. His first steps came at a small training ground, where he practised alongside boys of his age and those who were older. After a few months, he began training under a coach.
“I come from a small village where boxing was never a popular sport. Pooran Bohra sir was there. He trained a small group of boys for just a few hours on selected days of the week. But I was interested in learning. I listened to him carefully and repeated everything he taught me when I returned home,” Kapil said.
With time, Kapil developed as a boxer and competed in his first state-level competition in 2015. He went into the tournament with excitement but came away disappointed. His first competitive bout ended in defeat in the opening round.
“I was really disappointed. It was the first bout of my life, and I was seeing such a large crowd for the first time. I lost in the first round. But that competition and the defeat taught me a lot. My interest in boxing grew even stronger after that,” he said.
Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)
Kapil returned with a different mindset at the national-level competition. This time, he did more than win his bouts - he also claimed the gold medal. The prize money was followed by a job in the Indian Army. He joined the force in April 2017 and was appointed as a havaldar. His boxing career took a big step forward after that.
The Army gave him opportunities to improve his skills and compete at a higher level. He began training more seriously, took part in Services competitions, won medals and continued to grow as a boxer.
“My father wanted me to study and join the Army as a commissioned officer. He joined as a sepoy and retired as a havaldar. But he wanted me to reach a higher rank if I joined the Indian Army,” Kapil said.
“He was very happy. The day I won a national medal, he hugged me. That was when I realised that I had achieved something big in my life,” Kapil said.
“Now, after winning this Asian Games medal, I will be promoted to naib subedar. Papa said, ‘Ab tu mera senior ho gaya hai’,” the Indian boxer recalled with a smile.
Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)
The ‘Andre Russell’ of Khatima
Like many children in India, Kapil also grew up playing gully cricket. He even played inter-village cricket in Uttarakhand.
His height, muscular build and powerful hitting made him a popular figure on the local cricket grounds. His ability to hit big sixes earned him the nickname ‘Russell’, after West Indies power-hitter Andre Russell.
“I loved Andre Russell. I also liked Hardik Pandya. People used to call me ‘Khatima ka Russell’ because of my power. The boys wanted me in their team because I could hit big sixes,” he said, laughing.
Kapil Pokhariya (Image credit: Special arrangement)
The Road Ahead and LA 2028 Dream
For Kapil, the Asian Games bronze is only the beginning. His biggest dream is to represent India at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and win a medal.
Under the Boxing Federation of India's selection criteria, Asian Games medallists will be selected as the main entries in their respective weight categories for the 2027 World Boxing Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. The tournament is scheduled for April and will be the first qualifying event in boxing for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
Kapil knows there is still a long road ahead. “Rukna nahi hai ab, bas aage dekhna hai,” he said.
“The Olympics is the ultimate dream. I want to go there, represent my country and win a medal. That is the only thing on my mind right now. I am preparing for the World Championships in April,” he added.

briefs.headline: Kotian makes a case for Test call-up
briefs.deck: Kotian served national selectors yet another reminder to be considered for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy squad early next year
briefs.bodyText:
Despite yet to prove his T20 prowess, Tanush Kotian is stuck in a typical Indian cricket all-rounder’s quagmire: whether he is a batting all-rounder or a spin-bowling all-rounder. While the spinner insists he weighs both departments equally, the national selectors have often treated him in the latter category.
Kotian – with his career-best figures in an innings and in a match during Mumbai’s convincing win against Haryana – served national selectors yet another reminder to be considered for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy squad early next year.
“I don’t know about BGT, that’s up to the selectors,” Kotian said, adding he was not ruffled over Saransh Jain having been preferred as the India offspinner for the tour to Sri Lanka.
Never had Kotian bowled more than 65 overs in a match. To bowl in good areas consistently was as much a relief for him as his maiden ten-wicket match haul. “I was waiting for this opportunity. I was trying to bowl as much as I could. This is the first time I have bowled this much in a match. I am giving the captain confidence that I can bowl this much and can get that many wickets as well.”
Even before the season began, Kotian had stressed on having worked from exploring different angles and different variations while bowling. He showcased it plenty, bowling around the wicket consistently. Three of his eight wickets – Parth Vats, Aman Kumar and Ajith Chahal – came while bowling around the wicket.
Kotian elaborated on the bowling tips he received from Nathan Lyon during his brief stint with India’s Test squad in Australia in 2024-25. “(In Australia), you get extra bounce, so how can I bowl more over-spin balls, Lyon guided me. Also, with the run-up and how to use the over-spin. Whatever I learnt there, I am working on that and working with seam positions and variations, so that is helping.”

briefs.headline: Ranji Trophy: Vidarbha crushes Goa
briefs.bodyText:
Vidarbha bagged a valuable bonus point after winning its Ranji Trophy Elite Group-A match against Goa by an innings and 27 runs at the VCA Jamtha Stadium here on Thursday.
The host’s charge was briefly stalled by a fighting knock from Manthan Khutkar (70, 160b, 4x4, 5x6), but Harsh Dubey struck four times post-lunch to ensure that it ended victorious.
Khutkar and captain Abhinav Tejrana picked up where they had left off the previous evening, relentlessly blocking through the opening spell from Rajneesh Gurbani and Nachiket Bhute.
The first bowling change fetched a wicket as Yash Thakur bowled Tejrana while Snehal Kaunitkar fell soon after to Gurbani.
Lalit Yadav joined Khutkar, and the duo returned to a defensive approach until the latter launched Bhute for a six.
Khutkar took a liking to the left-arm spin of Parth Rekhade, hitting him for three sixes.
However, their hopes of survival were dealt a blow when Lalit’s attempted defensive shot ballooned into the hands of short-leg just before lunch. Dubey broke the game open after the break, tricking Khutkar and Yash Kasvankar into glancing catches to leg-slip, while Darshan Misal departed caught behind attempting to cut Aman Mokhade.
With defeat imminent, Shivendra Bhujbal managed to launch a couple of lusty blows, but Shubam Tari was run-out to seal a comfortable victory for the home side.

briefs.headline: ACT: India registers hard-fought victory over a spirited China
briefs.deck: Sukhjeet and skipper Harmanpreet score a brace each for the home team
briefs.bodyText:
India coach Craig Fulton had admitted that the Chinese team at the Asian Champions Trophy was unknown and it was difficult to plan against. India was clearly the better side but struggled to find the gaps before prevailing 5-2 on Thursday.
After the goal-fest against Bangladesh, India was up against a Chinese side with a very clear plan — pack the midfield, deny the home team space on the ground and force it to go in the air, then defend with everything they have. It almost worked, the Indians having to adapt, relying on their experience to enter not only the Chinese circle but also to keep them at bay.
A long aerial pass from India’s 25-yard line by Jugraj Singh was controlled just inside the circle by Sukhjeet Singh. He carried it a couple of steps ahead on the stick before unleashing a rasping hit over the head of the advancing goalkeeper Huanyu Wu in the 12th minute.
To China’s credit, its structure held firm with a counterattack and a couple of shots on goal. It finally levelled through Yang Peng’s penalty corner conversion in the 26th minute, only for Mandeep Singh to be checked on a counter and hand India a PC of its own. Harmanpreet Singh made no mistake to restore the lead.
The big positive was India’s sustained momentum either side of the break, something Fulton has admitted as frustratingly lacking. Two goals ins the first four minutes on resumption of action made it 4-1, Harmanpreet and Sukhjeet adding one each.
Another PC in the 36th minute for China and another goal made it 4-2 before Jugraj Singh got on the scoresheet with a PC.
Fulton would also be happy with India’s pace and the fact that not only the aerials were used to good effect but also the midfield’s ability to constantly rotate and stretch the opposition thin to move ahead.

briefs.headline: Former Dortmund star Schmelzer cherishes the battles with Bayern Munich
briefs.bodyText:
Marcel Schmelzer has featured in Der Klassiker on several occasions. He has played for Borussia Dortmund in 14 seasons of Bundesliga, after all.
Dortmund’s clash on Saturday with Bayern Munich would be a new experience for him. He would be watching the match along with Dortmund’s fans in Kochi, at Padma Theatre here.
Schmelzer, who is in the city for the Bundesliga ‘Z’ Football Week, is looking forward to the game. After ending his career as a defender at Dortmund in 2022, he has taken up a coaching job at the club.
The former captain has fond memories of Der Klassiker. “My most cherished memory is our 5-2 win in the Cup final in 2012,” he said. “It was an amazing game and an amazing season. I am hoping that we will get three points against Bayern on Saturday, too.”
Schmelzer, who played 16 games for Germany, is part of the Dortmund coaching staff that will conduct a clinic for local players and conduct workshops for trainers.
This is a joint venture by Zee Entertainment and Bundesliga Eagles FC as the local partner.
Eagle FC’s chairman Shaffi Mather said the response from young players and coaches was excellent. “We are glad that we could bring the Dortmund’s coaches to Kochi,” he said. “And Dortmund has a strong following here. There is a registered fans association for the club here.”
Suresh Letchmanan, Managing Director, Asia-Pacific, Borussia Dortmund, said developing young talent was an important part of the club’s philosophy. “We are delighted to bring our coaching expertise to Kerala, a region with a strong passion for football,” he added.
Former Dortmund and Australia midfielder Mustafa Amini is also part of the Dortmund delegation.

briefs.headline: Andhra’s bold move fails as Chhattisgarh triumphs
briefs.bodyText:
In a bid to force an outright result in its favour, Andhra lost even the one point it could have secured with a draw, as Chhattisgarh completed a five-wicket win in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group B fixture at the DVR Ground here on Thursday.
After losing the first-innings lead, Andhra asked Chhattisgarh to chase a tricky 179-run target with one-and-a-half sessions left. Visiting captain and opener Anuj Tiwary led from the front with a 60 off 73 balls (7x4, 1x6) before Ajay Mandal and Dev Aditya Singh finished the game in the extended period of play.
Anuj often came down the track to tackle the slow turn on offer and kept the scoreboard ticking with quick singles and occasional boundaries. Despite the loss of his wicket, Aditya and Mandal maintained the momentum to give Chhattisgarh its first win of the season.
Andhra skipper Ricky Bhui trusted his bowlers to defend the target after ending the second innings at 184 for three. Bhui scored an unbeaten 72 off 75 balls (4x4, 3x6) and was partnered by Karan Shinde, who followed his captain’s template and struck an unconquered 54-ball 53 (6x4, 1x6).
As soon as Shinde reached his half-century, Bhui declared the innings. He pushed for all six points after conceding the opportunity to take the first-innings lead, courtesy of Amandeep Khare’s unbeaten 89.
Chhattisgarh had needed 16 runs to go past Andhra’s 231, with only two wickets in hand, and Amandeep ensured it crossed that score. It was a small but vital advantage.
